headline: The ledger, its RLS and the balance view hold, and every API refusal is clean. But first run, the slice’s own journey, can’t be finished by someone with an empty account (RM0.00 can’t be typed), and it gets stuck after a lost answer while saving accounts. Three tests the slice made stale leave pnpm e2e and e2e:server red, and the first-run redirect has no test.

suites.unit: 480/481 (year scenario timed out at 5 s; passes alone in 3.1 s)
suites.security: pnpm security pass (audit, gitleaks over history, security lint); hygiene pass
suites.diff: 88 entries, 10 trees changed, 0 check findings, 6 metrics flags

findings.title: A balance of RM0.00 can’t be typed, so anyone with an empty account can’t finish first run
findings.detail: The money input drops leading zeros: `typedSen` in `packages/core/src/money.ts` strips `^0+`, so typing `0`, `000` or pasting `0.00` leaves the field `''`. First run's accounts step then refuses the empty field with *Type today’s balance, or 0.* There's no way to type the 0 the message asks for. An empty GrabPay Wallet or Ryt account is common, and the router holds an unfinished person at first run, so they can't reach Home except by going back and un-choosing that app (which stops capturing it). The owner's own phone step 4 in `docs/local.md` says *0 is fine for one that's empty*. The same input can't correct an opening balance to 0 in Account → Edit. The money input is B04's; the step that makes it a dead end is B08's.
findings.repro: Sign in as a capture person on the server preview → /s/first-run → Choose these → Next → Skip → Skip → type the other balances → tap GrabPay Wallet → type 0 on the number pad → Next

findings.title: A lost answer while the accounts save leaves first run stuck: Next again says *That app already has an account*
findings.detail: The accounts step sends one `account.add` per app, each with a fresh `newId()`. If an answer is lost (a dropped connection after the server saved it) or a later add fails, the step stays on 5. `runCommand` in `data/hooks.ts` only refetches after success, so the account list still lacks the saved account, and the next Next mints a new id for that app. The server refuses it with 409 `account_exists`, toasting *That app already has an account in Sen. Each app has one.*, and every further Next fails the same way. Only a reload (which refetches) gets past it. A retry should be a no-op (non-negotiable: every input has a dedupe key): the id per app should be kept for the step (in the draft), or the list refetched on failure.
findings.repro: FLOW-R: step 5, all four typed → Next while the 2nd account.add is answered by the server but the response is dropped (route.fetch then abort) → Next again

FLOW-R retry responses: ["409 {\"code\":\"account_exists\",\"message\":\"That app already has an account in Sen. Each app has one.\"}"]
FLOW-R toast: [ 'That app already has an account in Sen. Each app has one.' ]
FLOW-R accounts: ["Ryt Bank","TNG eWallet"]
waiting for getByText('Step 6 of 7') … element(s) not found

findings.title: Three tests the slice made stale leave `pnpm e2e` and `e2e:server` red
findings.detail:
The app behaves correctly in all three cases, but CI's suites fail on the branch (the handoff says the full `pnpm e2e` was left to QA):
1. `e2e/journeys.spec.ts` › balance-check expects *In 5 accounts*; D145 made the scenario 4 (the page reads *In 4 accounts*).
2. `e2e/production.spec.ts` › *B04's screens say Not built yet in production* still lists `/s/accounts` (and the other screens B08 made real); production now opens the real screen, which shows its error state with no server behind the test build.
3. `e2e/server.spec.ts` › *a session that ends while Sen is open…*: More now reads `/api/accounts` as it opens, so the ended session sends the person to sign-in (correctly, with *You were signed out*) before the test taps Settings, and the click times out on a detached element.
findings.repro: pnpm e2e (E2E_LOOKS=minted,copper); pnpm --filter @sen/web e2e:server after pnpm test:db

findings.title: The first-run redirect, D146 (2)'s rule that "could strand the owner", has no test
findings.detail: `firstRunDue()` in `router.tsx` decides who is held at first run. Breaking it to send *everyone* unfinished there, including capture people in a plain browser (exactly what D146 (2) forbids), leaves every suite green. The unit suite never loads the router. The fake backend skips `beforeLoad` (`__SEN_BACKEND__ !== 'api'`). `e2e:server` seeds only Wei Ming, with `setupDone: true`. My FLOW-1 step 1 and FLOW-10 now check (b) and (c) once; (a), in the shell, needs the phone.
findings.repro: In router.tsx replace `return !me.setupDone && (!me.capture || inShell());` with `return !me.setupDone;` → pnpm exec vitest run apps/web/src

findings.title: An archived account has no way back once its toast goes: no Archived list, no Add
findings.detail: Account → Edit → *Archive this account* removes it from Accounts with a 6-second *Undo*. After that, Accounts lists only live accounts, with no *Archived* section and no *Bring back* (Settings → Categories has both for categories). There's no *Add* either (handoff: not built), and first run's steps never come back. So one tap plus a missed toast loses the account and its opening balance from the app for good, while its app may still be chosen. Patterns: *Only a destructive action that can't be undone asks first*. Archive wasn't in the brief.

findings.title: The short first run offers *Cash* as a switch it can’t honour, and turning it off blocks *Start using Sen*
findings.detail: Without capture, first run lists the spending categories with a switch each; *switched off means archived*. Cash is a system category that can't be archived (D146 (6)), but its switch is enabled. Turning it off makes *Start using Sen* fail on `category.archive` with 409 `system_category`, and the person stays on *Step 2 of 2* until they find Cash and switch it back on. Cash's switch should be absent or disabled with its reason (patterns: a disabled switch says why).

findings.title: No test guards *balances use amount, not my_share*
findings.detail: Probe P2 made `account_balances` subtract `coalesce(my_share, amount)` for money out. pgTAP, the API tests and the catalogue all stayed green, because no fixture row on a balance account carries a share. §7 makes the separation explicit. B08 can't write a share yet, but B11's splits will, and the view is what Accounts and the agent read. One fixture row with `my_share < amount` in `ledger.sql` would catch it; then add the mutant below.
findings.repro: In 0014 replace the money-out sum with `sum(coalesce(t.my_share, t.amount))` → pg_prove ledger.sql rls.sql catalogue.sql on a fresh database

findings.title: Two breakage checks went stale: B08 rewrote the lines they break
findings.detail: `kept-after-sign-out` looks for `  writeStored(KEPT, null);\n}` in `data/api/backend.ts`, but `forgetKept` now has the first-run line after it. `no-hint-after-change` looks for `relay.hint(c.var.person.id, ['settings'])` in `routes.ts`, which is now a ternary with `ledger`. findings.title: *Finish* waits on the server with no spinner and no words
findings.detail: Pressing *Finish* dims the button for about 0.45 s (9 film frames) while `setup.finish` runs and every active query refetches. Then Home's skeleton shows. Patterns §7 *Waiting on the server* (and escapes E2) ask for a spinner and words such as *Finishing…*. The accounts step does it (*Saving…*); payday's Finish doesn't. This is also the measured cause of the metrics flag `step:first-run/18` (1601 ms): the dimmed button, then Home loading its data, which is over the 1000 ms limit on main too (standing `screen.settleMs`).
findings.repro: qa-artifacts film first-run/18.png (diff run), or tap Finish on step 7

findings.title: Offline at the accounts step, the banner promises *the rest waits*, but Next just fails
findings.detail: First run's offline banner reads *You’re offline. Signing in needs a connection; the rest waits.* At step 5, accounts go straight to the API (D146 (8)), so Next toasts *Sen can’t reach its server. Check the connection.* and stays put. The typed balances are kept, and Next works once online (FLOW-12 step 2 passes). The banner should say the accounts need a connection.

findings.title: The scan-after core journey failed twice under the metrics run on head only; a race on a transient screen
findings.detail: `journeys.spec.ts` › scan-after waits for *Reading receipt…*, a screen that's up for about 0.4–0.8 s. In the diff run's metrics (3 workers, CPU 4×, mobile network) it failed on head twice (metrics, film), and never on main. I walked it warm and throttled four times per side: the Reading screen showed every time, with overlapping windows (main 420–1359 ms, head 421–940 ms to Confirm). So it doesn't reproduce as a product difference. The assertion races the screen under load and should wait for Confirm instead.

findings.title: More asks `/api/accounts` for people without Capture, and gets a 403 every time
findings.detail: More calls `useAccountList()` before checking capture, so a person without Capture triggers a refused request on every visit. Nothing shows, but it's a wasted round trip, and it's why the session-end test in finding 3 now trips on More.

findings.title: From reading only (not run): a reopened accounts step shows each account’s computed balance as if it were its opening
findings.detail: `Accounts` in first-run.tsx builds `openings` from `AccountRow.balance`, the view's computed balance. In B08 they're equal (no transactions). From B09, a person who goes back to step 5 after captured payments sees the moved balance, and a re-save would write it as the opening, keeping the old `opening_at`. AccountView has `opening`; the list doesn't.
